_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING for ChkParseData, each with the argument behind it. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object, so the claim and its reason live in one file, and a declared mutant LEAVES THE DENOMINATOR -- every entry is a claim somebody has to be able to answer. FOUR are declared and EIGHT survived; the other four are NOT declared, are named in evidence/ChkParseData/README.md, and are the reason this unit's score is not 1.000. The test applied to each is the one units #1 and #4 wrote down: a survivor is equivalent only when NO input can make it change an output -- not when this corpus happens not to. Three of the four here are a BUFFER DECLARED ONE BYTE LARGER, which is the one shape where that test has a proof rather than a search: the extra byte is never written and never read, because every write and every read is bounded by a separate constant the mutation did not touch.
3452e325: index_offset `char FndUCVarName[UCVarNameLen]` -> `[UCVarNameLen + 1]`. The buffer becomes 21 bytes. Every access to it is bounded by `UCVarNameLen`, which this mutation does NOT change: `char_assign(FndUCVarName, UCVarNameLen, ...)` writes exactly 20 bytes (memcpy of min(len_src, 20) then memset of the remainder to 20), `conv2uc_c(FndUCVarName, UCVarNameLen)` reads and writes exactly 20, and `ftrim(FndUCVarName, UCVarNameLen)` reads exactly 20. Byte 21 is written by nothing and read by nothing on any input, so no input distinguishes it. The DIFFERENT mutant `'20' -> '21'`, which changes the bound as well as the buffer, is NOT declared and did survive -- see the README.
4dd65c7d: index_offset `char ExpUCVarName[UCVarNameLen]` -> `[UCVarNameLen + 1]`. The same argument as 3452e325, on the other local. Both are listed rather than one being called `the same as the other`, because they are two mutants and each is its own claim.
7b3ecc9f: index_offset `char lineNumStr[Int2LStrLen]` -> `[Int2LStrLen + 1]`. The buffer becomes 12 bytes. `int2lstr_c(FileLineNum, lineNumStr)` writes exactly 11 -- that count is compiled into the generated Fortran bridge (`DO vit_ri_int2lstr = 1, 11`), not read from this declaration -- and `ftrim(lineNumStr, Int2LStrLen)` reads exactly 11. Byte 12 is written by nothing and read by nothing. Again the constant-changing sibling `'11' -> '12'` is NOT declared: it moves the READ bound onto a byte the bridge never writes, which is a different mutant with a different answer.
56ae9c62: swap_call_args `std::min(len_src, len_dst)` -> `std::min(len_dst, len_src)`. `std::min` is symmetric in its arguments for a total order, and `int` is one. The two expressions denote the same value for every pair of ints, so no input can distinguish them -- this is an equivalence in the strict sense and not a statement about the corpus. It exists as a mutant at all because `std::min` replaced a written-out `(len_src < len_dst) ? len_src : len_dst`, which had a mutable `<`; the trade was deliberate (one truly-equivalent mutant instead of one unobservable one) and is argued in the translation.
